title: Terms on the Number of Medical Records Requests a Patient May Hold
content:
**Clause.** A patient may have any number of Medical Records Requests over time, for different recipients, different record scopes and different date ranges. There is no maximum number of requests per patient. Where a patient's requests overlap, the overlap is governed by the Medical Records Requests rule on open duplicate requests and free copies.

## The clause in its parts

| Point | What the clause provides |
|---|---|
| Who | The patient whose records are requested. |
| How many requests | Any number over time; no maximum per patient. |
| What may differ between requests | The recipient, the record scope and the date range. |
| Overlapping requests | Governed by the rule on open duplicate requests and free copies. |

## Basis questions

**Does a patient who already has a Medical Records Request lose the ability to open another?** No. The number of requests a patient may hold over time has no maximum; a further request for a different recipient, scope or date range is a request in its own right.

**Hypothetically, may one patient over a year hold a request for their own copy, a later request sending records to a treating provider and a third request for a different date range?** Yes. The three differ in recipient, scope or date range, and no count limits them. Whether any two of them overlap is a matter for the rule on open duplicate requests and free copies.
